title: Latency and error rate use different denominators
summary: This reference defines latency over 12,000 completed requests and error rate over 12,500 attempted requests. The snapshot date is September 22, 2026; metrics with different denominators must remain separate.

sections.title: Definitions for completed-request latency and attempted-request error rate
paragraphs: Median and 95th-percentile latency include completed requests only. Requests that end in error are excluded from the latency distribution but remain in the error-rate denominator.
Error rate is the share of all attempted requests that end in error. The two metrics therefore use different denominators even when they cover the same period.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Latency uses completed requests; error rate uses all attempted requests.
figures.accessibleDescription: In the illustrative September 22, 2026 snapshot, median latency was 180 milliseconds and 95th-percentile latency was 420 milliseconds across 12,000 completed requests. Error rate was 1.8 percent across 12,500 attempted requests.

quotations.text: Do not read latency calculated without failed requests and error rate across all attempted requests as if they shared one denominator.
quotations.originalText: 오류 요청을 빼고 계산한 지연 시간과 전체 요청 오류율을 같은 분모처럼 읽지 않는다.

limitations: All numbers are illustrative and exist only to exercise the report contract.
This example defines metrics; it does not assess the performance of a real service.
Comparability changes when the percentile method or reporting window changes.
